title: Centrifuge

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)
Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: Spins samples at high speed to separate components by density (e.g. pelleting cells from a suspension) using centrifugal force.
operatingPrinciple: Rotation generates centrifugal force proportional to rotor radius and the square of rotational speed; denser components move outward/downward faster than less dense components, separating them (see the RCF ⇄ RPM Calculator for the underlying relationship).
basicOperation: Balance the rotor by loading matched, symmetrically opposed tubes of equal mass.
Select the appropriate speed/time/temperature for the task, following the specific protocol being used.
Allow the rotor to come to a complete stop before opening the lid.
importantSettings: Speed (RPM) or relative centrifugal force (RCF/×g) — these are related but not interchangeable without knowing rotor radius (see RCF ⇄ RPM Calculator).
Run time and, for temperature-sensitive samples, chamber temperature.
calibration: Rotor-specific maximum speed ratings and periodic maintenance checks per the manufacturer's schedule; never exceed a rotor's rated maximum speed.
maintenance: Keep the rotor and chamber clean and dry.
Inspect tubes/rotor for cracks or wear before each use.

commonErrors.problem: Excessive vibration or noise during a run
commonErrors.fix: Stop the run, rebalance tubes with matched masses on opposite sides of the rotor, and restart

commonErrors.cause: Speed/time insufficient for the sample, or incorrect rotor radius assumed when converting RPM/RCF
commonErrors.fix: Confirm the correct RCF for the protocol and verify rotor radius used in any RPM/RCF conversion

safety: Never open the lid while the rotor is still spinning.
Always balance loads before starting a run.
Do not exceed the rotor's rated maximum speed.
